findings.issue:
Number literals inside the arrays of `type`, `required`, `dependentRequired` and `dependencies` escape the number bounds. The library's own meta-schema check parses them with math/big, so a schema of a few hundred bytes makes CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build run for seconds per keyword, or panic.

Probes: scratchpad r6spec/p/ (zz_r6meta_test.go), run with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 -overlay <scratchpad>/r6spec/p/overlay.json -run 'TestR6MetaNumbers' -v ./internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/` on 4 vCPUs.

(1) Slow compile, 241 bytes. `{"type":[1e999999,2e999999,...,20e999999]}` (20 distinct literals): CompileSchema takes 11.2 s, then returns RZ-CFG-005 from the meta-schema ('value must be one of ...'); about 380 math/big parses at about 30 ms each.
- `{"properties":{"a":{"type":[...20 x e999999]},"b":{"required":[...20 x e999998]}}}` takes 22.5 s.
- `{"$defs":{"a":{"type":[4 x e999999]}}}` takes 0.40 s in CompileSchema and 0.35 s in Check.
- Cost is linear in the number of such keywords, so a 256 KiB document can hold hundreds of them.

(2) Panic. `{"type":[1e9999999,...,21e9999999]}` (21 literals, hash path): CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build each panic with 'invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference'; trace math/big/rat.go:412 <- jsonschema/v6.writeHash util.go:399 <- duplicates util.go:350 <- arrValidate validator.go:344 <- the meta-schema anyOf.
- Same panic for `{"required":[...]}`, `{"dependentRequired":{"a":[...]}}`, `{"dependencies":{"a":[...]}}`, nested arrays `{"type":[[1e9999999],[2e9999999],...]}`, and a member map a reference reads as a schema: `{"$ref":"#/x/properties","x":{"properties":{"type":[...21 x e9999999]}}}`.
- Nothing in the package recovers the panic, so a ~250-byte Policy crashes `ruralz validate` and the Node's stage H unless a caller WP-51 does not own catches it. Such a schema should get RZ-CFG-005 at the literal.

No test or fuzz seed covers numbers in these keywords; the walker never looks at their values.
findings.fix:
Apply the number bounds to every value the library's meta-schema check can parse, before anything compiles: the whole value of `type` when it is an array; the whole value of `required`; every member value of `dependentRequired`; every array-valued member of `dependencies`. Check these at every schema position, including reference targets and member maps read as keyword trees. Use checkNumbers on those values only, not on schema-valued `dependencies` members, so 07 req 76 still holds (annotations and unknown keywords are never refused). Cheaper alternative with the same effect: refuse any non-string entry of these arrays at the walk (RZ-CFG-005 'must be strings'), since the meta-schema refuses it anyway.

Correct doc.go:45-48 and 515 to name these keywords. Add regression tests citing R-77 and 07 F6: each shape above is refused with RZ-CFG-005 at the offending literal, with no panic, through CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build; the 20-literal e999999 `type` case is refused by the walk (shown deterministically with TestPatternParsesBounded-style counting). Add seeds to FuzzCompileSchema.

findings.issue:
The matcher charge covers the backtracker's visited bit set (at most 32 KiB) and the NFA queues, but not the backtracker's job stack. Go uses the backtracker for every program of at most 500 instructions whenever the string or member name is shorter than 262,144/len(prog) bytes. The job stack holds one 16-byte job per alternation state on the current search path and can grow to about 2^17 to 2^18 jobs; with append growth the old and new arrays are live together, so the peak is about 4 to 7 MB per match, while the charge stays at 32 KiB + 64 bytes per instruction (about 33 to 64 KB).

Measured through Factory.Build and Handle at the 10 MiB default with peakHeap/peakExchange; scratch tests TestR6Backtrack, TestR6Concurrent, TestR6Shapes built with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c -overlay <scratchpad>/r6/p/overlay.json ./internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/`:
- {"type":"string","pattern":"a*b"}, body a string of 43,688 'a' (43,690 B): 400 at /pattern; reserved 125,832 B; heap peak 2,195,456 (17.4x); decision pass allocated 3.59 MB.
- {"type":"string","pattern":"(?:(?:a??){240}a)*b"} (486 instructions, within MaxPatternInstructions), body a string of 537 'a' (539 B): reserved 97,440 B; heap peak 5,758,976 (59x); decision pass allocated 11.3 MB. Work charged 4.19e6 of 2.68e9 units, so the work bound does not limit concurrency.
- Same pattern under patternProperties, body object of 645 member names of 531 to 533 bytes (346,901 B, valid): reserved 529,781 B; peak 7,364,608 (13.9x). Under propertyNames, the failing case reserved 777,565 B with the same peak.
- Concurrency with the 539-byte body against one Filter: 50 requests, summed reservations peak 4.87 MB vs heap peak 115.5 MB (23.7x); 200 requests, 17.3 MB vs 239 MB (13.8x); 1,000 requests, 48.1 MB vs 304.5 MB.
The Node-wide maxBufferedBytes therefore admits thousands of such requests (512 MiB / 97 KB) while each holds several MB nothing reserved, bypassing the bound R-77 relies on. CPU is not the issue (0.35 to 0.61 ns per charged unit).
findings.fix: Charge the backtracker's job stack wherever a pattern may reach a string or member name of n bytes, only when the reaching pattern's program has at most 500 instructions and n < 262,144/insts: 16 bytes x min(alts x (n+1), 2^18), times about 2.25 for old and new arrays during append growth, where alts is the program's InstAlt count recorded per pattern in patternCost next to insts, and the document-wide flag keeps the largest alts among backtrack-eligible programs. Alternatively, charge a flat 2^18 x 16 x 2.25 (about 9.4 MB) whenever such a pattern may reach a value of at least 262,144/insts/alts bytes. Correct the matcherBytes comment, doc.go 'Working set' (transient copies) and the regexcost.go header. Add a Handle regression test with (?:(?:a??){240}a)*b on a 539-byte string and a*b on a 43,688-byte string, asserting peakHeap <= reservation + gcSlack.
findings.evidence:
I reproduced this on the current working tree (Go 1.27.1, linux/amd64). The probes were scratch tests overlaid into the package: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/0aabfe6e-34a6-51d2-9b9b-23886b703760/scratchpad/v1/probe_test.go and probe2_test.go, built with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c -o <scratch>/js.test -overlay <scratch>/overlay.json ./internal/filter/validation/jsonschema/`. Afterwards the repository showed only the untracked files that were already there.

**Through Factory.Build and Handle at the 10 MiB default** (buildFilter with limit 0, peakHeap and peakExchange, the package's own helpers):
- `{"type":"string","pattern":"a*b"}` with 43,688 'a' (6 instructions, so maxBitStateLen is 43,690 and the backtracker is used): 400 at /pattern. Reserved 125,832 B; heap peak 2,285,568 B (18.2x); 3.69 MB allocated.
- The same pattern on a valid body of 43,687 'a' plus 'b': the result is Continue. Reserved 125,744 B; peak 2,015,232 B (16x). Valid bodies are affected too, not only failing ones.
- `{"type":"string","pattern":"(?:(?:a??){240}a)*b"}` (486 instructions, 241 InstAlt, maxBitStateLen 539) with 537 'a': 400 at /pattern. Reserved 97,440 B; peak 5,775,360 B (59x); 11.34 MB allocated.
- Both single-request cases break the package's own invariant `peak <= reserved + gcSlack` (1 MiB), which TestHandleBoundsUnevaluatedMemory and the other tests in working_test.go use.

**The match alone, outside the Filter:** `regexp.MustCompile(noOnePass+expr).MatchString` gives the same peaks, 2.0 MB and 5.78 MB, with 3.44 MB and 11.33 MB allocated. The memory belongs to Go's regexp itself, not to the library's other structures.

**Concurrency on one Filter with the 539-byte body:**
- 50 requests: summed reservation peak 4.58 MB vs heap peak 95.2 MB (20.8x).
- 200 requests: 12.2 MB vs 223.4 MB (18.4x).

**Cause.** In `$GOROOT/src/regexp/backtrack.go`, `shouldBacktrack` is `len(prog.Inst) <= 500`, and `maxBitStateLen` is 256K / len(prog.Inst). `bitState.jobs` grows by append, one 16-byte job per InstAlt visit on the DFS path, so it can reach up to about 2^18 jobs. compilePattern (patternsize.go:103-112) only prepends `(?:)` to block the one-pass matcher, so the backtracker stays eligible.

**What the code charges.** working.go:80-82 says matcherBytes + matcherInstBytes cover "its queues per program instruction and the backtracker's visited set". working.go:1001-1006 charges a transient of 32 KiB + 64*maxInsts. Nothing covers the job stack.

**Requirement.** 07 req 80 says "the decision pass's working set ... is reserved beside the decoded values". R-77 bounds memory per request through that reservation. Here the decision pass holds several MB that nothing reserved. No deviation or OQ row in the WP-51 run records (w3-s2b-result.json, w3-s2-wp51-r1/r3/fix-result.json) covers the backtracker job stack; the earlier matcher findings dealt only with when the matcher is charged and with program size.

contractRequests: 07 req 75 and architecture R-77 (F1): record how a pattern's program is measured. It is Go's parser estimate of its instructions, every copy of a repetition included, plus the ranges of each Unicode class escape (\p, \P) at five ranges per instruction. The escape ranges are counted at the size of each escape's table as the parser builds it (\pL is 659 ranges). A pattern whose escapes alone exceed MaxPatternInstructions is refused before it is parsed. Also record the new proposed RZ-CFG-005 rule: the case-insensitive character-class ranges of a document's patterns may span at most maxFoldRunes = 131,072 characters together. Go's parser folds such ranges one character at a time, about 3 ms per [\x{42}-\x{1e942}] under (?i), so 1,000 of them took 3 s before any compile.

Architecture R-63/R-77 and docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md 'Body buffering and limits' (S8 row; F3): the 12x reservation limit is now enforced. Decoded values at the jsonval charge, plus their map, array and string overhead, plus the decision pass's working set over 12 times maxRequestBodyBytes is 413 RZ-RT-003 before Reserve. A failing body whose location pass would take the reservation past 12x gets DetailMismatch alone. The request side therefore holds at most 13x (130 MiB at the default). At the default, arrays of one-member objects are admitted up to about 25% of the limit (20% with a bounded integer member). Note for the spec owner: R-63's jsonval charge leaves out object hash tables and array spare capacity. Message.Decoded (WP-43) and other consumers reserve the jsonval charge only, so for such bodies they under-reserve by up to about 3.3 times the decoded limit.

Architecture R-77 and the S8 rows in the performance and configuration documents (F2): please cite the measured fit at the 10 MiB default.
- Records: 81% and line items 70% (decoded-limited).
- Tags, strings under a pattern and long strings: the full limit.
- One-character enums: 31%; 250-value enums: 34%.
- Events under an 8-way oneOf: 32%; under a 20-way oneOf: 13.6%.
- GeoJSON polygons: 14.7%.
- Rich text: 20% (paragraphs only) and 4.7% (mixed blocks with nested lists).
- Component-tree row: 6.2%; a component tree 6 deep with 3 children per node (27 KB) passes, 7 deep (80 KB) does not.
- uniqueItems arrays of objects: about 6,600 objects (2.3%).
- Map under propertyNames: over 60%.
Also record that the decision pass is reserved at its worst case over the library's member order. Valid union or recursive documents therefore reserve 3.5 to 11 times their measured peak at those sizes, and up to about 70 times for small, deeply nested ones. The call stack is charged 8 KiB per evaluation of one in-place chain per value.

Architecture R-77, 07 req 75 and the RZ-CFG-005 rows of docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md (Pattern measure): record how a pattern is measured against MaxPatternInstructions and MaxDocumentInstructions. (a) A character class counts 1 + ranges/5 instructions in every copy a repetition makes. (b) The parsing work counts too, measured lexically before the parse: Unicode class-escape table ranges at 2 per instruction and case-folded characters at 8 per instruction. Measured costs: merging and sorting escape ranges in a class takes about 0.11 µs a range, folding about 31 ns a character, and Go's compile 0.2 to 0.4 µs an instruction. The separate maxFoldRunes refusal of the previous round is removed. Review shapes: 98 x ^\pL{990} kept 864 MB; a 19,000-range class repeated {990} took 3 to 6 s. Both are now refused before compile.

Architecture R-77 and 07 req 75 (Meta-schema checks, proposed): record two rules. (1) MaxSubschemas counts a position again for every meta-schema check the library repeats on it, and the bytes such repeated checks cover are capped at MaxSchemaBytes. A check repeats when a reference names a position whose keywords hold subschemas already checked, such as #/x/properties. (2) maxCheckCopies = 2^19: each reference target outside the keyword tree that the library checks apart costs a copy of its bookkeeping (positions + 2 x resources + anchors). Measured: 2,040 such targets took 1.1 s and 574 MB; the largest accepted shape takes about 0.35 s. Ancestor ladders cost one check because the compile checks targets ancestors-first; before this they took 5.3 s and 2.2 GB. Add OQ-configuration-model rows, or amend req 75.

07 req 77 (carry-over across Policies): a Policy new to a snapshot has no BuildEnv.Previous. If it builds before a carried-over Policy with the same document, it compiles the document again; the carried-over Policy now adopts that Schema, so the snapshot still holds one Schema per document. The extra compile cannot be avoided inside WP-51. Either record that this depends on build order, or have the snapshot compiler (WP-70) expose the previous snapshot's shared values by key, so a new Policy can reuse a compiled document.

Architecture R-77 and 07 req 90, replacing the S2 compile request's figures and R-77's 9 MB: a worst-case validation.json-schema compile takes under about 0.7 s (0.54 to 0.7 s at load 1 to 3) and allocates up to about 330 MB. Its heap peaks at about 35 MB, the collector's pacing included. The compiled Schema keeps up to about 16 MB: about 10 MB for MaxSubschemas positions of the library's compiled schemas (about 2.4 KB each) and about 6 MB for patterns at MaxDocumentInstructions. Please record 16 MB, not 9 MB, at S8.

R-77 and 07 req 75, patterns (Open question row): the library's regexp engine compiles every pattern behind an empty group (?:), so Go never builds its one-pass matcher. Matching is unchanged. Anchored patterns run on the backtracker or the NFA, which the work model bounds. The pattern measure counts what the compiled pattern keeps, in 40-byte instructions: the instructions Go estimates, every copy included; the class ranges, once (5 per instruction); 3 per literal or class node; and 24 per pattern. It also counts the parser's work. This replaces R-77's literal rule ('a pattern whose compiled program exceeds 2^14 instructions'), and docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md should state it.

07 section 9 item 21 and the work bound: record the new terms.
- 1 unit per 8 bytes of each member name per hash: once per evaluation with member keywords, 5 per unevaluated copy, uniqueItems sorting and lookups, and once per uniqueItems comparison.
- Per 8 bytes of the object's longest name, 1 per const or enum object compared with it.
- 1 per 8 bytes of the required and dependency names an evaluation looks up.
- 2 units per queue entry, byte and search step in a pattern's largest class.
BenchmarkWorkModel stays at or below 0.75 ns per unit, so the 2.7 s bound at the 10 MiB default still holds.
